text:
maria gonzalez: quick heads up — after enabling cross-zone spillover for the regional queue policy were seeing p95 token latency in eu-west increase from ~220ms -> ~360ms for longer sequences (~8k). suspect batching + KV-cache behavior.
eric li: yep saw the same. traces show larger, more variable batches when spillover is on. also more KV cache misses when requests hop clusters.
rajiv: can you paste the profiling output you looked at? flame/allocs/kv stats?
maria gonzalez: small excerpt: ```
profiler: batch_formation: avg_batch_tokens=512, tokens_std=210
kv_cache_miss_rate: +12% (vs baseline)
kernel_selection: 87% fast_attn_v2, 13% fallback->generic_attn for sharded shards
```
eric li: interesting — fallback to generic likely explains some of the tail. note we force `prefer_same_zone:false` in the policy (we wanted max utilization). maybe we should try `prefer_same_zone:true` + spill_threshold=0.75 to limit cross-zone mixing. token_budget_target is 640 right now — that might be too aggressive for EU traffic profile.
rajiv: proposed experiments:
- control: current global policy
- variant A: prefer_same_zone=true, spill_threshold=0.75, token_budget_target=480
- variant B: keep prefer_same_zone=false but reduce token_budget_target=320, and prefer quantized kernels when spilling

maria gonzalez: ran a 5% canary with variant A last night for ~3h: p95 improved (260ms) but throughput dipped ~3%. variant B reduced GPU cost but increased short-query p95 by ~5%.
sre-bot: Incident logged: deployment 2025-06-11 08:14 UTC caused perf regression in eu-west. ref INC-3421. :warning:
deploy-bot: rollout metadata: region=eu-west, policy=crosszone-fanout-v2, commit=9a3f2c
eric li: KV cache angle — cross-zone fanout increases cache shard diversity. requests that used to hit the same cache now miss and rebuild KV, causing extra latency. idea: add a sticky prefix routing TTL so the same convo stays in one cluster for N seconds to keep the KV warm.
rajiv: aggree. sticky routing + cap max_spill_tokens could help. e.g. `sticky_ttl=120s` and `max_spill_tokens=256` to prevent huge cross-zone batches. also we should instrument kernel fallback reasons (capability mismatch vs mem pressure vs seq length).
maria gonzalez: implemented a prototype queue policy: 
```yaml
regional_queue_policy:
  prefer_same_zone: true
  spill_threshold: 0.75
  token_budget_target: 480
  sticky_ttl: 120s
  max_spill_tokens: 256
```
initial A/B: kv_miss -6% vs baseline, p95 ~245ms on canary. tail (p99) unchanged for now.
eric li: next steps: enable `kernel.trace=on` in runtime config to capture fallback reasons for 24h. collect metrics: kv_miss_rate, p50/p95/p99, cost_per_token, batch_size_distribution. run microbench with 1k synthetic convo shapes to tune token_budget_target.
rajiv: also add a lightweight hist of `batch_token_variance` per queue to dashboard, helps detect pathological mixing quickly.
maria gonzalez: i'll open config PR, add dashboards, and attach profiler traces to INC-3421. plan: roll variant A -> 30% for 12h capturing metrics; if stable bump to 70%.
eric li: sg. ping me when PR is up and ill run the microbench harness against the canary buckets.
maria gonzalez: thanks — will do. :thumbsup:
